newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: EU must augment aid with action, commissioner says.
newsitem.headline: EU must augment aid with action, commissioner says.

text.p: The European Union must supplement humanitarian aid with concerted political action if it is to provide an adequate response to crises in the world's trouble spots, European Commissioner Emma Bonino said on Tuesday.
Bonino, who is the commissioner responsible for the European Community Humanitarian Office (ECHO), said the EU had failed in the past to match aid with action.

"Most of the member states are really not willing to put together their will when it comes to foreign policy and even defence and security policy," she told Irish radio during a visit to Dublin for a conference on aid.
"But crises are so complex nowadays that no member states alone can give an adequate response, be it from the financial point of view, politically or even militarily," she said.

Bonino said the humanitarian office was unable to solve crises on its own. "We never thought that we can solve political crises. We can just save lives, buying time for other actors to solve the political problem," she said.

"The problem was that humanitarian aid was there but the other actors were not there in the last few years to do their job," Bonino said. "We have been the only actors in the field, waiting for the others to take up their own responsibility, which they didn't do."

The EU must take its wider responsibilities seriously, she said. "We must not simply say the Union is agriculture plus common market plus single currency -- these are good but not good enough to give a new dream and a new hope to our people."
